SAMPLE: AdMob and the User Messaging Platform are built in. Ad requests wait for onboarding, a successful current-session consent update and SDK initialization, and are suppressed for ad-removal owners. Required privacy options are available in Settings. Debug always uses official test ad identifiers. Specify actual advertising data processing in your final policy.

SAMPLE: Firebase Analytics is built in but collection defaults to off. Only an explicit current-version opt-in can enable collection in a configured release. Debug and unconfigured builds do not initialize Firebase. Analytics consent does not grant advertising consent. Adapt your final disclosure to actual events, identifiers, processors, retention and deletion rights.
SAMPLE: Replace sample dates and describe how meaningful policy updates and renewed consent will be handled.
SAMPLE: Determine your intended audience before enabling production services. Configure age-appropriate ads, consent and Play declarations. This starter does not implement an age assurance flow.
SAMPLE: Optional analytics can be disabled in Settings. Ad privacy options appear when the provider requires them. Explain the scope and limits of withdrawal in your final policy.
SAMPLE: Replace the placeholder developer identity and contact links in brand.xml with working details before publication.
SAMPLE: Describe any legal disclosures and data-sharing arrangements applicable to your app. Do not assert practices that have not been verified.
SAMPLE: Google services and any developer links you configure have their own terms and privacy policies. Document each processor and purpose actually used by your app.

SAMPLE ONLY. Replace this document with your app-specific privacy policy before publication. Identify your developer, purposes, data recipients, retention, rights and contact information. The following describes the starter, not future features.

SAMPLE: Preferences store your language, appearance, consent and cached purchase status. App-only logs remain in memory; recent crash records are stored privately. Report export and APK sharing happen only when requested. Review reports before sharing; they may contain sensitive information.

SAMPLE: The starter uses network access, optional notification permission and the Nothing Glyph SDK permission. Glyph controls require supported hardware and release the service when leaving the screen. No privileged device access is included.
SAMPLE: Set and document actual retention for app data and each service. The starter keeps a bounded crash history and cache exports; deleting app data clears local preferences.
SAMPLE: Users can change analytics and advertising privacy choices in Settings. Define jurisdiction-specific access, deletion and complaint processes and a functioning contact channel.
SAMPLE: Describe reasonable safeguards accurately. Do not promise absolute security. Never ship private keys or account credentials.
SAMPLE: You choose whether and where to share app logs, diagnostic archives or the installed base APK. No automatic report upload is implemented. Split APKs may not install on their own.
SAMPLE: Explain where your actual providers process data and the safeguards required for your users.

SAMPLE: Define how users will be informed of material changes.
SAMPLE: Provide your legal developer identity and a working contact channel in brand.xml.
SAMPLE: Explain any user-content functionality you add. This starter has no account or cloud content service.
SAMPLE: Define the audience and eligibility requirements appropriate to your app and jurisdiction.
SAMPLE: Have any indemnity clause reviewed for the actual app and applicable law.
SAMPLE ONLY. These example terms are not legal advice or final app terms. Adapt them to your app, audience, jurisdiction and business before publication.
SAMPLE: Identify the rights holder for your app. Preserve third-party attribution. No Nothing or Google endorsement is implied.
SAMPLE: Specify the correct governing law and dispute process only after legal review.
SAMPLE: Obtain qualified advice before writing warranty or liability limitations. Mandatory consumer rights cannot be waived by sample copy.
SAMPLE: Retained source is subject to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and third-party terms. These sample app terms do not replace those licenses or authorize commercial reuse. Obtain appropriate rights.

SAMPLE: Adapt severability and other provisions to the actual agreement.

SAMPLE: The retained non-consumable product identifier is remove_ads. No products or prices are created by this starter. Google Play provides configured prices, payment handling and owned-purchase restoration. Pending purchases do not grant entitlement.
SAMPLE: Publish a complete app-specific privacy policy. Optional analytics and advertising privacy choices are separate.
SAMPLE: Nothing Glyph controls depend on supported hardware, firmware, authorization and device settings. Stop controls at any time; other device content can take priority.
SAMPLE: Define service availability and termination terms suitable for the actual app.
SAMPLE: Google Play, AdMob, Firebase and Nothing SDK terms may apply to their respective functionality.
SAMPLE: App updates are distributed through Google Play. There is no self-updater or installation permission.
SAMPLE: Describe permitted use of your app without claiming nonexistent functionality.

Google Firebase Analytics receives automatic usage events, device and app details, an installation identifier and IP-derived approximate location to help understand app usage. No custom events are added. Collection starts only if you enable this switch and continue. You can disable analytics in Settings. Advertising choices are separate.

Development safeguard: official Google test ads only. Firebase Analytics cannot initialize or transmit in this debug build, even if you opt in. Your preference is saved for release.

Matrix uses in-app display mode, not a background toy. A running toy or device setting can take priority. Phone (2a) Plus uses an on/off strip fallback because SDK 2.0 lacks progress for that model. Leaving this screen releases the lights.

The Nothing service could not connect, authorize or display content. Check your app API key, Glyph settings, SDK debug mode and firmware. Lights have been released; you can retry.
Lights idle. No device service is bound.
Control Nothing lights and matrix progress on supported phones.
This device matches the SDK hardware list. Service authorization and compatible firmware are still required. Controls affect only the lights while this screen is open.
Glyph and Matrix controls are unavailable on this device. A supported Nothing phone running Android 14 or newer is required. Other app features work normally.
